positions.name: Global X Uranium ETF
positions.thesis: The purest listed claim on the fuel bottleneck. Holds miners and enrichers, so it captures the spot uranium move with equity beta stacked on top.
positions.breaks: A restart of idled Kazakh and Namibian supply, or one high-profile reactor incident, resets sentiment far faster than mine supply can respond.

positions.name: VanEck Uranium & Nuclear ETF
positions.thesis: Deliberately the boring half of the fuel pair. Weighted toward utilities and reactor builders rather than juniors, it earns cash while URA takes the risk.
positions.breaks: It is not really a uranium proxy — the utility weighting means it can drift with rates while the actual fuel thesis plays out.

positions.name: Petrobras PN
positions.thesis: Pre-salt barrels at a single-digit multiple with a double-digit payout. Priced for permanent political risk, which is a real risk that is nonetheless already in the number.
positions.breaks: Dividend policy is set by the controlling shareholder, and the controlling shareholder is the state. Fuel-price intervention ahead of an election ends the thesis without warning.

positions.name: Saudi Aramco
positions.thesis: The lowest-cost barrel on earth and the swing producer that sets the floor. Owned as the stabiliser of the bucket, not for its growth.
positions.breaks: Free float is thin and the payout leans on the state budget. A sustained sub-$60 Brent forces a choice between the dividend and Vision 2030.

positions.name: LandBridge Company
positions.thesis: The hinge of the thesis, held at an ordinary 5% line because a small float makes it one of the book's most fragile names. Owns Permian surface acreage and collects royalties on whatever sits on it — water handling, pipelines, and now data-centre leases. Sells energy and compute demand without drilling or buying a GPU.
positions.breaks: Small float, and the data-centre revenue is a handful of contracts. Concentration cuts both ways: it fell 9.5% in a single session on 12 Aug 2026.

positions.name: Nebius Group
positions.thesis: A neocloud: rents GPU capacity by the hour to firms that will not build their own. Sits in this bucket because the binding constraint on the business is contracted power and shell space, not chips.
positions.breaks: Classified here as a power consumer, which is a stretch — it is really a compute landlord. Capex-funded, customer-concentrated, and competing with hyperscalers who own their own silicon.

positions.name: CoreWeave
positions.thesis: The scaled version of the same trade as NBIS, with a contracted backlog rather than a spot book. The clearest listed read on whether AI capacity is genuinely pre-sold.
positions.breaks: Debt-funded purchases of an asset that depreciates on a chip cycle. One anchor customer renegotiating resets the whole model, and it overlaps heavily with NBIS — this is one position expressed twice.

positions.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
positions.thesis: The actual bottleneck. Nearly every accelerator in this book is fabricated by one company, so this is the least substitutable position in the portfolio.
positions.breaks: A Taiwan Strait event is not a drawdown, it is a permanent impairment — and the same event takes ^KS11 and 2357.TW with it. The single largest correlated risk here.

positions.name: Advanced Micro Devices
positions.thesis: The only credible second source of accelerators. Owned as the option on buyers refusing to accept a single supplier, not as a bet on it winning outright.
positions.breaks: The moat is software, not silicon. If CUDA holds, competitive hardware still does not convert into share, and the share gains are already in the multiple.

positions.name: Palantir Technologies
positions.thesis: The application layer. Sells the deployment of models into government and commercial workflows, which is where the margin sits once inference is a commodity.
positions.breaks: The multiple is the position. Growth is real and accelerating, but at this valuation a single decelerating quarter costs more than the growth adds.

positions.name: Vanguard Information Technology ETF
positions.thesis: Broad exposure to the complex, so the bucket survives being wrong about any single name.
positions.breaks: It already holds AMD, TSM's peers and the megacaps, so it overlaps with half this bucket. It dilutes single-name risk without adding a new bet — closer to a cash proxy with tech beta than genuine diversification.

positions.name: ASUSTeK Computer
positions.thesis: AI server exposure at a hardware multiple rather than a semiconductor one. The AI server business is repricing the whole company while it is still classified as a PC maker.
positions.breaks: Server assembly is margin-thin with real customer concentration, and the legacy PC cycle still swamps the AI line in reported revenue.

positions.name: iShares MSCI South Korea ETF
positions.thesis: Country-level exposure to memory, held through the MSCI Korea fund. HBM pricing runs through Korean national accounts, and the market carries a persistent governance discount that is finally being addressed.
positions.breaks: It is not the KOSPI: MSCI's 25/50 caps hold Samsung and SK Hynix below their index weight, and the fund trades in New York hours against a Seoul close, so a year can open a double-digit gap to the Korean market in either direction.
positions.trackingNotes: MSCI Korea 25/50 caps single names, so Samsung and SK Hynix are held below their KOSPI weight; EWY also trades in New York hours against a Seoul close, and carries a 0.59% expense ratio.

positions.name: iShares AI Infrastructure UCITS ETF
positions.thesis: Spreads the infrastructure bet across semis, cloud and networking, including names the single-name lines here miss.
positions.breaks: Overlaps with VGT and with the megacap complex most portfolios already own, and the LSE line quotes GBP against a USD NAV — an FX layer sitting on top of the actual exposure.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: The hedge against the financing of everything above. If the buildout is funded by deficits and suppressed real rates, gold is the direct expression of that — and as spot-backed shares it carries no expiry and no roll.
positions.breaks: Pays nothing to hold. A genuine real-rate spike is its enemy, and it can fall alongside risk assets in a liquidity event precisely when the hedge is needed.

positions.name: Avantis International Small Cap Value ETF
positions.thesis: The deliberate opposite of the rest of the book: ex-US, small, cheap, profitable, and largely unowned by the AI trade. Here to be uncorrelated, not to be exciting.
positions.breaks: Value has underperformed growth for most of a decade. If the buildout simply keeps compounding, this is a permanent drag.

positions.name: JPMorgan Chase
positions.thesis: The lender to the buildout. Captures capital-markets activity and a steeper curve without taking a view on which operator wins.
positions.breaks: Imperfect ballast: it is levered to the same economy the rest of the book needs, so it fails in the scenario the hedge exists for. A credit cycle hits it and the neoclouds together.

positions.name: Investo MVIS Global Rare Earth & Strategic Metals
positions.thesis: The materials upstream of everything else here: magnets, motors, turbines. Exposure to export controls on rare earths, which is the supply chokepoint the compute bucket cannot design around.
positions.breaks: A concentrated, policy-driven, high-beta commodity-equity basket that will likely fall with the rest of the book rather than against it — and it is a thin BRL listing carrying currency risk on top.

positions.name: iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: US Treasury bills maturing within three months: the closest listed thing to cash that earns the policy rate. It does not rise when AI falls; it simply does not fall, and it is intact and liquid when everything else is not.
positions.breaks: Deep Fed cuts shrink the yield toward zero, and inflation above the yield erodes it in real terms. A US debt-ceiling standoff is the one event that can briefly dent bills themselves.

positions.name: State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF
positions.thesis: The S&P 500's consumer-staples companies: food, drinks, household goods and the retailers that sell them. Demand for toothpaste does not depend on data-centre capex, and money leaving AI has historically rotated here.
positions.breaks: Still equity: it fell 24.5% in the 2020 crash. Walmart and Costco are a fifth of the fund, tobacco a tenth, and GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are a slow threat to food and beverage volumes.

thesis.variantView: The market prices the AI buildout as a semiconductor story and treats power as a utility input that will be supplied on demand. This book's view is that grid interconnection, fuel and sited land are the binding constraint for the next three to five years, so the scarce rent accrues to whoever owns power, fuel and land with grid access rather than to the designers of the chips; the consensus reprices that only once announced data-centre capacity visibly slips.
thesis.horizon: Three to five years, matching transformer, switchgear and interconnection-queue lead times. Daily and monthly moves are monitored, not acted on.
thesis.reviewRules: Reviewed each quarter against the portfolio falsifiers below and every line's own 'what breaks it'. A line is cut when its falsification condition is met, not on price alone; a line whose valuation breaches its bucket's trim rule is cut back to target. If two portfolio falsifiers trigger in the same quarter, the thesis itself is reconsidered, not just the lines.

checks.name: Hyperscaler capex cut
checks.test: Two or more of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta cut next-year capital spending guidance in the same quarter.

checks.name: Compute keeps leading power
checks.test: Compute out-returns Energy by more than 20 percentage points over twelve months.
checks.detail: Compute minus Energy, twelve months, USD

checks.name: Uranium price breaks
checks.test: Sprott Physical Uranium Trust (a holder of physical uranium) falls more than 25% over twelve months.

checks.name: Memory pricing rolls over
checks.test: Micron, the listed read on HBM pricing, trades more than 30% below its twelve-month high.

checks.name: Oil floor gives way
checks.test: Brent trades below $60, the level at which Saudi Aramco and Petrobras payouts come under pressure.

stress.note: Historical windows use each line's own USD total-return series where it existed at the window start, and the stated proxy otherwise. Book loss is today's weights held through the window (no rebalancing). Benchmarks are shown over the same dates for context.

stated.name: Grid Bottleneck
stated.premise: Interconnection queues and transformer lead times, not chips, become the binding constraint on new capacity. Announced data-centre build slips.

stated.name: CapEx Retrenchment
stated.premise: Hyperscalers cut AI capital spending guidance. The supercycle is re-rated as a cycle.

stated.name: Geopolitical Shock
stated.premise: A Taiwan Strait escalation. Advanced foundry output is interrupted and export controls tighten on strategic materials.

costs.note: Stated assumptions for the net-of-cost series, not quotes. trade_bps is commission plus half the bid-ask spread per dollar traded, by listing currency. fx_spread_bps is charged on every dollar traded in a non-USD line. withholding_pct is charged on each distribution as if held by a non-US individual investor without treaty relief; interest-related dividends from US T-bill funds can be exempt in practice, so SGOV's drag is overstated, and Brazilian JCP (15%) is ignored. Fund expense ratios are already inside fund prices and are not charged again.
